sample_scope.ranking_basis: public listing rounded view counts; ties unresolved

Ranking Best Roller Skate Moments Ever 😭

not_collected.reason: age-restricted; YouTube sign-in required; cookies not used by policy

sample_scope.note: popular = top 10 within public listing of 99 videos at collection time (rounded view counts), not verified all-time ranking

material_policy.rule: One narrow physical-situation theme per video (trampoline, trampoline park, skate, skateboard, strong wind, wasp nest, chicken scream, jumpscare, lights-off, ankle break). Every clip is a short third-party clip of the same situation.
counterexamples: pC-YhohIz20: title says chicken scream, but the ranked clips are mixed falls; the chicken appears only as a reaction cutaway

material_policy.rule: Each clip has one visible payoff event in 2-5s (fall, launch, collision, scare, fold, theft by wind) that a single word can name.
counterexamples: pC-YhohIz20 #6 (hand reaching to plank) and #3 (pedal POV) have no clear event in the frames

material_policy.rule: Use 6 clips (5-7). Total length 22-33s, median about 24.5s.
Harm stays comic: people get up, fall into foam/water/mats, or are startled. No visible serious injury in any ranked clip.
counterexamples: HSGNOINpHgk #4 ends with the skater under a pickup truck (outcome not shown)

material_policy.rule: Credit the source creators: on-screen @handle above the watermark, or the list in the description.
counterexamples: pC-YhohIz20, zw6ugKBs3rM, Yd4rZBecs3U, t4hPHmGEqco, GyD9EScGnbQ: no handle seen on screen; descriptions title-only or not reported

story_transformation.rule: Cold open: clip #last plays from t=0 with only the title; the list appears at ~0.94-1.4s with the first label already filled in. The viewer is in the action before any explanation.
The empty, coloured #1-#3 slots stay visible from the start: a built-in 'what will be #1?' open loop that keeps people watching to the end.
Labels accumulate: earlier labels stay on screen, so the list builds into a mini recap of the jokes so far.
Escalation ladder: lower ranks are single small mishaps; middle ranks are bigger launches or folds; #2 and #1 are the largest impact or scare.
counterexamples: HSGNOINpHgk #1 is a calm mantis, not the biggest crash
GyD9EScGnbQ #1 is the one clean removal after chaotic ones
t4hPHmGEqco #1 is a toddler bumped by an inflatable, smaller than #5 launch

story_transformation.rule: What earns #1 (the twist): (a) biggest single impact/scare (HSQ33Rl3nqA tarp, Dx_Hc7m8n08 traffic cone, Yd4rZBecs3U grin close-up, pC-YhohIz20 merry-go-round group fling); (b) a format break that recontextualises the list (HSGNOINpHgk mantis, GyD9EScGnbQ clean removal, GbDgCzsjvqQ the save); (c) an 'impossible' skill or glitch moment framed as admiration (JohsrvlOuhA Spider-Man, zw6ugKBs3rM Noclip, r9xvl94-_z4 Iconic); (d) a cute-victim contrast (t4hPHmGEqco toddler).
The #1 label often flips tone from mockery to mock-admiration (cool or praise emoji: sunglasses, fire, relieved face, pleading face).
counterexamples: pC-YhohIz20, GyD9EScGnbQ, Yd4rZBecs3U, Dx_Hc7m8n08 end on skull-style #1 labels

story_transformation.rule: The #1 clip is usually not the longest; only about 3 videos make #1 clearly the longest.
No narration or voice-over; the story is carried only by order, labels, and source-clip audio.
Occasional inserted gag that literalises a label or the topic: Netflix logo after 'Netflix' (t4hPHmGEqco 14.6-15.7s), chicken reaction cutaway after #3/#2/#1 (pC-YhohIz20).
counterexamples: the other 10 show no such insert

narrative_recipes.name: Nickname ladder with admiration twist
narrative_recipes.input_conditions: 6 clips of one situation, each with one clear event; at least one clip with an 'impossible' or stylish moment.
narrative_recipes.setup: Cold open on the weakest mishap; list with empty coloured slots appears ~1s.
narrative_recipes.progression: Small mishap -> launches/folds -> biggest crash at #2; labels alternate literal, understatement and character nicknames.
narrative_recipes.line_roles: Each label reframes its clip as a character, object or game event; earlier labels stay as a running joke list.
narrative_recipes.screen_rules: Persistent 2-line title, left list, label at clip start, one emoji, hard cuts.
narrative_recipes.payoff: #1 is the stylish or impossible moment with a praise nickname (Next Spider-Man, Noclip, That save, Iconic, Aura farming) and a cool emoji.
narrative_recipes.exclusions: Clips with real injury; clips needing speech to understand.

narrative_recipes.name: Escalation to the biggest hit
narrative_recipes.input_conditions: Clips that differ clearly in size of impact or scare.
narrative_recipes.setup: Mildest clip first under a deadpan or literal label.
narrative_recipes.progression: Each rank bigger than the last; vine boom on 1-2 mid-rank impacts.
narrative_recipes.line_roles: Understatement for lower ranks (Went for a walk, Humbled), stronger name for top.
narrative_recipes.screen_rules: Same template; scare videos may use black frames from the source.
narrative_recipes.payoff: #1 = largest physical hit or scare reveal with a big-name or death label (Captain Jack Sparrow, Traffic cone, R.I.P).

narrative_recipes.name: Percentage meter
narrative_recipes.input_conditions: Similar clips where intensity or satisfaction is the joke (screams, nest removals).
narrative_recipes.setup: Lowest percent (10-15%) with skull or cool emoji.
narrative_recipes.line_roles: Numbers only + one emoji; the emoji carries the tone.
narrative_recipes.screen_rules: Same template; optional recurring topic cutaway (chicken).
narrative_recipes.payoff: #1 = 100% with skull; the clip is the most extreme or the cleanest (GyD9EScGnbQ).
narrative_recipes.exclusions: Do not mix nickname labels into a percent video.

narrative_recipes.name: Format-break #1
narrative_recipes.input_conditions: One clip that breaks the pattern (animal, controlled success, toddler) among 5 fails.
narrative_recipes.setup: Five ordinary fails with mixed labels.
narrative_recipes.line_roles: #1 label names the break with a meme or game term (Aura farming mantis, Critical hit, 100%).
narrative_recipes.payoff: Surprise that the winner is not the worst fall.
narrative_recipes.exclusions: Do not use if the break clip is not funny on its own.

types.type: pop-culture / game / meme nickname (calls the person a character or game event)
types.when_to_use: When the body pose or motion visibly resembles a well-known character, film scene, or game mechanic; strongest for #1 and #2.

types.type: literal action nickname (names the shape or result)
types.when_to_use: When the event has one clear shape (folding, launching, spinning, ending under a car). 'Folded' recurs in 4 videos (JohsrvlOuhA, t4hPHmGEqco, zw6ugKBs3rM, r9xvl94-_z4).
When the fall is harsh but harmless; the deadpan line contradicts or shrinks what we see.
When the joke is the audio or the viewer's own reaction; good for scare and sport clips.
When a fall looks like a cartoon gag (limbs flailing, flat splat).
When the clips are similar and the joke is intensity or satisfaction; whole video uses only percentages, ending at 100% on #1.

rules.rule: 1-4 words, English, sentence case, no punctuation except rare dash/period.
The label names a reading of the clip, not a description of it: it tells the viewer how to see the event (as a character, an object, a game event), so it works as the punchline.
Usually one trailing emoji; skull is the most common; cool/fire/relieved emojis tend to appear on #1.
counterexamples: no emoji: Loyal Skates, Broke him in half, Had him in splits, His head fell off-, Straight through the floor, HEE HEE

rules.rule: Mix label types inside one video (except percent videos); no video uses one type for all 6 nickname labels.
Percent ladders rise monotonically and end at exactly 100% on #1; middle values 67% and 85% repeat across both percent videos.

counterexamples: GbDgCzsjvqQ #2 label changes from 'ahh slip' to 'Cartoon ahh slip' mid-clip (typed-in reveal)

upload_title_rule.rule: 'Ranking {Adjective} {Topic} {Moments|Fails|Challenge|Removal|Scream}' + optional 'Ever' + one emoji. Emoji: crying 7, laughing 4, skull 1. Adjective: Funniest 5, Best 5, Satisfying 1, Craziest 1.
counterexamples: final noun: Moments 6, Fails 3, Challenge/Removal/Scream 1 each

on_screen_title_rule.rule: Same words as the upload title, no emoji and no 'Ever', split into 2 centered lines: line1 'Ranking'(white) + adjective(yellow); line2 topic keyword(blue, may be 2 words) + category noun(white). Bold with black outline, on for the whole video.
counterexamples: pC-YhohIz20 line2 'Chicken Scream': Chicken blue, Scream white (no category noun)

layout_measured_640.note: fonts unidentified; Pretendard used as substitute

label_on_clip_start.rule: Each label appears at or shortly after its clip starts (typically 0.1-1.5s), while the event is still to come; the label primes the joke before the payoff.

clip_length.rule: Clips ~2.3-7.8s, most 3-5s. Even-interval ladder in some videos (fosJO6N-NMo, HSQ33Rl3nqA about every 3-4s).

cuts.rule: Hard cuts between clips; no rank-number transition card. Rare flash/radial effects of unknown origin.
counterexamples: zw6ugKBs3rM speed lines 16.5-17.5s and black frame 6.2s

vine_boom.rule: Myinstants 'VINE BOOM SOUND' (waveform match only, not ear-checked) on the impact or scare-reveal frame inside a lower-ranked clip, 0-4 per video (usually 1-2), never on the #1 clip in this sample, never on label pop.
counterexamples: 5/12 have none: Dx_Hc7m8n08, HSQ33Rl3nqA, JohsrvlOuhA, pC-YhohIz20, t4hPHmGEqco
GbDgCzsjvqQ stacks 3 hits in one clip (#6, 1.14/2.24/3.01s)

level.rule: Mixed near full file level: gain vs file -2.9 to +0.6 dB (12 hits), one at -5.8 dB (fosJO6N-NMo); mix RMS about -4 to -7 dBFS, typically 3-13 dB above the previous 2s, so the boom clearly sits over the clip audio.

other_sfx.rule: Second shared sound pC-YhohIz20 2.6s / GyD9EScGnbQ 8.76s (r 0.85) in 2 videos only; unidentified, not a channel rule. No other repeated SFX verified. Background music presence unknown.

audio.original_audio: kept (all 12 samples carry clip audio; ASR shows original speech)

engines.cpb render_preview: not used: narration-centric, mutes original audio, no rank list

korean_adaptation_proposed.rule: Title in 2 lines with the same colour roles: line1 '{형용사} 순위' style e.g. '가장 웃긴' (yellow) + '순위'(white); line2 topic (blue) + category noun such as '모먼트/실패/챌린지'(white). Upload title the same words + one emoji (😭/😂/💀).

Labels 2-8 Korean characters, one emoji; mix 별명(영화·게임·밈 캐릭터: 스파이더맨, 토르, 마리오), 동작 별명(접힘, 발사, 헬리콥터), 절제 표현(괜찮음, 아주 푹신, 산책 감), 반응어(아야, 노노, R.I.P). Use percentage ladder 10%→100% only for similar-clip themes. Prefer references Korean viewers know; keep game terms like '크리티컬' that cross over.
Keep no narration; labels only. Label pops at clip start, vine boom on the impact frame of 1-2 lower-rank clips, not #1, near file level.
Do not reproduce the POLARRANKS watermark or claim labels are the original creators' words; credit source @handles on screen at y~544 or in description.
Plan #1 deliberately: pick the biggest impact, a format-break clip, or an admiration-twist clip, and write its label last after the others are set, so it contrasts with the ladder.
